intended_object: For a family (S_i) of objects in a k-linear abelian category with a grading-shift autoequivalence, the matrix whose (i,j) entry is the bigraded Ext Poincaré series Σ_{n<b, p} dim_k Extⁿ(S_i, S_j{p}) · (n,p), truncated below cohomological degree b (Beilinson–Ginzburg–Soergel §1.2, 2.11). I took this from the docstring and the module documentation.
explanation:
The definition fills in each entry separately: entry (i,j) is `bigradedExtPoincareSeries k e (h i j) b`. That series is the finite double sum over n < b and over the finite internal support of `single (n, j) (finrank k (GradedExt e X Y n j))`. Its coefficient lemma (`coeff_bigradedExtPoincareSeries`) confirms that the coefficient in bidegree (n,j) is dim_k Extⁿ(X, Y{j}) when n < b and 0 otherwise. This is exactly what the docstring describes.

- **Truncation:** cutting off below b matches the docstring, and the library proves the matrix does not depend on b once b is past a vanishing bound (`bigradedExtPoincareMatrix_eq_of_le`).
- **Finiteness hypothesis:** the hypothesis `IsGradedExtInternallyFinite` is what makes each slice a finite sum, so that the series is a finitely supported element of ℕ[ℤ×ℤ].
- **Generality:** the setting is already general. It is any k-linear abelian category with Ext and any autoequivalence playing the role of the shift, and any index type I.

Mathlib has no bigraded Ext Poincaré matrix, so there is no counterpart to cite.
